stem:
Irfan builds two shapes from the same 6 unit squares, side-aligned with no gaps. Shape P is a 2-by-3 rectangle. Shape Q is an L-shape made by moving one square.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Both shapes have area 6 square units; their perimeters can differ.
Both shapes have the same perimeter because each uses 6 unit squares.
Moving the square changes the area; the perimeter stays the same.
Equal area for these 6-square shapes also forces every polygon of any size to share one perimeter.

teacher.key_rationale: Same number of unit squares means same area. Perimeter depends on how many edges are shared, so the L-shape can differ from the 2-by-3 rectangle. B treats square count as enough for perimeter. C swaps area and perimeter. D over-extends the equal-area idea.
